content:
CASCO in Moldova is voluntary insurance for your own vehicle on agreed conditions. It does not replace RCA and does not promise payment for every mechanical fault. For a 2027 comparison, establish the vehicle, required risks and repair arrangements before deciding which premium looks better.

Editorial revision: 26 November 2026. The 2027 scenarios are planning examples, not forecasts or confirmation of individual insurance terms.

The National Bank of Moldova’s contract guide explains contract components and questions for reading conditions. Checked 26 November 2026; it does not confirm a particular product, tariff or 2027 terms.

Who should review the policy?

The assessment is useful when losing the vehicle or paying for substantial repairs would disrupt personal finances or a company vehicle budget. A financed vehicle also needs review against the lender's particular requirements. Acceptance by a lender does not prove that a proposal meets every need of the owner. Check the beneficiary and arrangements for using a payment.

Declare the actual use: personal journeys, deliveries, taxi work, rental or company operations. Ask about permitted drivers and countries before travelling. Describing a commercial vehicle as exclusively private to simplify a quotation creates an inaccurate basis for comparison.

Which risks and repair terms matter?

Request answers on collision, theft, natural events, glass damage and third-party actions. The CASCO label alone does not establish that every event is included. Discuss added equipment, keys, storage and the required steps after an incident separately.

Ask how repairs are authorised, which workshops can be used, what parts are specified and whether depreciation applies. Establish how a major loss is valued. A lower premium says little about the repair arrangement or the expenses you may retain. Have unclear conditions explained before payment rather than relying on the workshop's expectations.

How is the price calculated?

The premium is the amount paid for insurance. Assessment may require make, model, year, value, use and driver details. MOLDASIG’s CASCO quotation form asks for vehicle and driver details. Checked 26 November 2026; this is an assessment-input example, not a tariff, universal discount or coverage confirmation.

This guide has no verified standard CASCO tariff for 2027. Request a current calculation specifying risks, period, currency and territory. The deductible is the loss portion borne by the insured under the contract. Compare it for each relevant event where the document uses different arrangements. An advertised rate without those details is not a like-for-like comparison.

Which exclusions need clarification?

Ask about mechanical breakdown, wear, previous damage, undeclared use and circumstances involving keys. These are questions to verify, not a universal exclusion list. Supply accurate information and retain any inspection record required by the proposed procedure.

Read notification and repair-consent requirements. Do not substitute a deadline from another insurer's online guide. People's safety and instructions from competent services take priority over collecting photographs; this article gives no technical emergency instructions or guarantee about repair costs.

Planning for 2027 and later

Review changes in drivers, value, vehicle use and travel territory. For an electric car, ask specifically about the traction battery, electrical damage and charging accessories. A vehicle policy does not automatically include a fixed charging station at home or at company premises.

Three situations for a practical decision

These examples are entirely hypothetical and do not describe real customers. They show what to check and which records to prepare; no risk acceptance or payment is implied.

  • Situation: A newly purchased car is financed. What to check: Compare lender requirements with your own questions about repairs, the beneficiary and deductibles. Lender acceptance does not replace reading the conditions. Document: The financing requirements, final proposal and repair arrangements.
  • Situation: A used vehicle has previous damage. What to check: Describe its condition accurately and clarify valuation, inspection and separation of existing from later damage. A requested market value is not an agreed compensation amount. Document: Registration information, condition records and value evidence requested by the assessor.
  • Situation: An electric car will be used abroad. What to check: Check the battery, countries and workshop arrangements. Describe a fixed home charger separately from vehicle accessories. Document: The specification, intended countries and a written response identifying the objects considered.

Prepare registration and ownership or use information, vehicle and driver details, the existing policy and known damage. Request the final quotation and full conditions. An enquiry or completed website form does not itself establish that insurance has begun.

Practical prevention

Before renewal, reconcile driver details, actual use and vehicle information. Organise key and document handling without publishing security arrangements. Vehicle maintenance and insurance serve different purposes; technical roadworthiness needs competent assessment rather than an inference from the policy.

Frequently asked questions

What information should I prepare for a CASCO quotation?

Prepare vehicle, ownership or use, value, driver, actual-use and travel-territory information. Disclose known damage and supply the existing policy where relevant. Ask whether an inspection or additional evidence is required instead of importing another proposal’s document list.

How should I compare price with deductibles and repairs?

Compare accepted events, the owner’s contribution, workshops, parts, valuation and territory. Where deductibles differ by event, review each arrangement. A lower premium without these answers does not establish that a proposal is more suitable.

How should I handle repairs after damage?

Prioritise safety and competent services’ instructions. Then identify the notification and repair-authorisation procedure in your own policy and retain relevant records. This article gives no universal deadline and does not promise acceptance of repairs ordered independently.

What should an electric-car owner ask for 2027?

Request written answers about the traction battery, electrical damage, charging accessories and workshop arrangements. Distinguish vehicle property from a fixed charging installation. These are individual-assessment questions, not a new-product announcement or premium-growth forecast.

How can I check exclusions before buying?

Ask about wear, breakdown, previous damage, keys and actual use, then match the answers to the particular conditions. Mentioning a scenario does not establish that it is always excluded or always accepted. Resolve the unclear point before deciding.
